title: Quote arguments correctly
goal: Keep literal text, expansion and filename boundaries distinct.
challenge: Use the supplied filenames and a variable containing two words. Demonstrate literal versus expanded values, a quoted wildcard, safe glob expansion and quoted command substitution. Preserve the literal backslash and prove literal command-like text did not execute.

steps.explanation: Create a unique learner-owned guest workspace. Stop if creation or cd fails. Retain its printed path; variables do not survive disk Resume.
steps.expected: A fresh directory inside the guest home; no existing files are changed.

steps.command: value='two words'; printf '%s\n' alpha > 'red note.txt'; printf '%s\n' beta > 'back\slash.txt'
steps.explanation: Single quotes protect literal filename characters.
steps.expected: Two files with the exact stated names.

steps.explanation: Single quotes suppress expansion. Double quotes permit variable expansion as one argument. A quoted * remains literal.
Filename expansion creates complete arguments; quote a variable holding a path. This includes quoted.txt created in the previous step. No match normally leaves the pattern literal.

steps.command: here=$(pwd); printf '<%s>\n' "$here" > location.txt; printf '%s\n' 'literal $(touch surprise)' > literal.txt
steps.explanation: Command substitution executes pwd in the guest. Single-quoted command-like text remains data; never use eval to reinterpret it.
steps.expected: location.txt identifies this workspace; no surprise file.

steps.command: cat literal.txt; test ! -e surprise; printf 'literal status=%s\n' "$?"

hints: Which expansions still occur inside double quotes?
Compare actual output, immediate exit status and resulting files. A syntactically valid command or script can still do the wrong thing.
Keep the original, verify a small intended change, and demonstrate rollback inside this workspace.
review: I retained the stated observations and can explain the outcome.
I checked failure cases and preserved originals; my review is not an application-verified score.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 partial 103.1, 103.3 globbing. Reinforcement is labeled; no full-objective mastery. Completion records self-review, not verified assessment. No score.
